pull_request.title: Tracker: Propose common pixel endcap disc supports and routing
pull_request.head: design/pixel-endcap-support
pull_request.body:
The current pixel endcap staggering leaves too little room for a conventional local support beneath some modules. This draft develops a common disc support, mounting rails and cable/CO2 routing, with public ATLAS/CMS engineering references and reproducible screening.

Proposed architecture: one 6.3 mm carbon-fibre/foam sandwich per disc, short graphite thermal feet, ten independently metered titanium half-ring circuits, and three kinematic mounting stations on rails bonded to a closed carbon carrier. All 18 discs reuse the same 112-quad x/y pattern. No production geometry or working active layout is changed.

The alternative using a single backplate at the current sensor positions is retained and screened. The preferred mechanical concept requires a separately reviewed z/face staggering amendment and a 3.5 mm outward shift of the first disc/collector on each end. These remain proposals; coverage/ACTS validation must precede adoption.

Review artifacts:
- [DES014 design](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/pixel-endcap-support/docs/design/DES-014-pixel-endcap-support.md)
- [Results and explicit limitations](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/pixel-endcap-support/docs/validation/DES-014-pixel-endcap-support/results.md)
- [Five-sheet drawing book](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/pixel-endcap-support/docs/validation/DES-014-pixel-endcap-support/drawings.pdf)
- [Literature dossier](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/pixel-endcap-support/docs/design/inputs/DES-014-literature.md)
- [Repeatable workflow](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/pixel-endcap-support/tools/pixel_endcap_support/README.md)

Measured/screened results:
- Zero module/pickup/foot envelope overlaps; minimum pickup-to-neighbour gap 0.20 mm. Pipe transitions, fixtures and flex artwork are not validated swept solids.
- About 594 g local passive assembly/disc, including provisional flex and full-liquid tube mass; about 2.169 kg shared carrier/rails per end. Annulus-normalized equivalent inventory 1.635% X0; not a directional material scan.
- 1.204 kW/disc nominal and 18.2 g/s proposed CO2 flow. Stress exit quality <=0.430, below the 0.45 arithmetic ceiling. Hydraulics remain unqualified.
- **Thermal stress target fails:** the reference edge-biased pickup model gives about -16.6 C nominal and -4.9 C at 1.5x load, versus a -15 C target. The heat path needs improvement; this PR does not declare cooling adequate for adoption.
- Including the current PR35 barrel handoff, reference trunk utilization reaches 96.7%; conservative/stress cable scenarios fail. Last-disc bypass adapter and fixed-sector routing remain open.

Validation: 10 new controls pass, including an analytic heat-conduction case, energy conservation, inverse-conductivity scaling, mirror symmetry and deliberately rejected layouts. A second execution reproduces scientific JSON and 13 artifacts byte-for-byte; source/code/artifact hashes are checked. Dashboard validation/build and relevant tests pass after correcting the evidence registration; session records validate. No native DD4hep, ACTS, material scan, structural FEA or hydraulic test is claimed.

Governing work: DES014, DES002, DES010/011, DES013; relates to module issue #7. Updates project tracking, reconciles merged PR35 metadata and records sources/commands/limitations. No design sign-off is recorded. Exact token counters are unavailable for this task.

issues.title: Design reusable RD53 pixel-module alternatives
issues.body:
Develop DES-001 as a stand-alone RD53 pixel-module proposal with reusable structures, few module types, low material and realistic manufacture, services and thermal interfaces. The available RD53 chip is fixed; the exact inventory variant is being clarified. Pixel volume/layer layout is not selected by this task.

The Tracking Engineer leads two independent alternatives, each with top-view and cross-section drawings, source facts/derivations/design choices and explicit limitations. The Project Coordinator supplies a balanced comparison and conditional recommendation after technical synthesis.

Public RD53 documentation and ATLAS/CMS detector/upgrade TDRs are references, not an instruction to copy either experiment. Catalogue every new normative source in reference/manifest.yaml, distinguish RD53A from production successors, and leave unverified thickness/power/irradiation assumptions visible. Include active/inactive area, chip tiling, bumps, flex/adhesive/bonds, sensor bias/isolation, material accounting and credible cooling/power/data handoffs. Layout fit, radiation requirements, engineering tolerances and production sign-off remain separate gates.

Scope: DRAFT designs and source/design study evidence only; no detector geometry or reconstruction changes. Update project tracking in the same PR. Existing context: stage B/C of PLAN-NODD-001, global envelope baseline DES-003 / ADR-006, with the formal-sign-off documentation discrepancy preserved.

events.text:
Assistant outcome (paraphrase): inspect the actual 18-disc baseline; compare a
retained-position backplate with a support-driven stagger amendment; develop a
common sandwich disc, rails, carrier and routing concept; retain thermal and
service-capacity failures instead of presenting a qualified design.

An optional question asked whether revised staggering could be proposed. No answer
had arrived when preparing the draft. B is therefore explicitly a **proposal**;
no baseline geometry or acceptance state is changed and no approval is inferred.
No subagents were used for this bounded task.

events.text:
DES014 remains DRAFT/PROTOTYPE. All discs have the same x/y pattern:112 quads,
448 chips, five radial rows. Candidate A's narrow central posts fit but have a
poor optimistic thermal lower bound; increasing their width causes collisions.
Candidate B uses a common 6.3 mm carbon sandwich, two routing planes, ten CO2
half-ring circuits, 0/1.65/3.30 mm local support heights, a three-point coupling
and rails bonded to a closed carrier shell. B keeps counts, x/y and IDs, but
proposes new sensor z/mounting faces and a 3.5 mm first-disc/collector shift.

The initial two-level inner-ring trial collided with next-nearest neighbours;
three levels resolve the tested body intersections. Two crossing 2.8 mm pipe
planes require more than the initial 3.5 mm plate reservation; the documented
6.3 mm prototype is retained. Neither exploratory input was an approved baseline.

Final local module/pickup/foot envelope checks have zero overlaps. The heat/quality
balance passes its 0.45 ceiling, but the pickup-temperature stress screen fails.
The current-barrel-plus-endcap reference trunk uses about97% of available area;
adverse bandwidth scenarios fail. Pipe transitions, interfaces and flex artwork
remain conceptual. The mass estimate includes curved tube saddles, displacements,
provisional flex and full-liquid local coolant; it is not a solid-model measurement.
Five original drawing sheets, a PDF book, source dossier, placement comparison,
configurable model, regression controls and exact source/artifact hashes are retained.
PR35 merge metadata was reconciled without inferring new design approval.

events.text:
The selected DES015 layout controls the text, including the updated barrel and
common two-face endcap support. Earlier alternative studies are not narrated.
Engineering approximations remain briefly visible as properties of the preliminary
layout. The chapter uses source-derived vector figures and explicit source
locators, rather than inventing dimensions or treating generated pictures as data.

Local TDR editing is authorized by the user's direct request. Its README says
“Do not push”; the remote was not updated. A parent-repository source snapshot
and PDF make the content reviewable without moving the gitlink to an unpublished
commit. Human review and any later publication remain distinct actions.

events.text: PubDoc preliminary PixelDetector subsection — see the canonical narrative for outcomes and checks.

User requested a larger text block with less margin; internal nODD decisions
must be explained in the TDR rather than cited; barrel services in Figure 2.1;
use the compact-module SVG from unmerged PR #8 to inform Figure 2.3; cables and
color legend in Figure 2.5; color legend in Figure 2.8.

Text width increased from 124 to 150 mm; side margins 43→30 mm, top 32→25 mm,
bottom 41→28 mm. Body fonts/leading remain readable and unchanged. PubDoc rewrote
the two chapter files to incorporate physical rationale and leave seven public
bibliography entries. Internal decisions, generated inventories and PR revisions
are preserved in source provenance, without publication citations. The rationale
covers module interfaces, guards, populations, support and spreader widths, tube
loads, ring restraint, alternating disc faces/heights, pickups, carrier and cables.
The already-catalogued NIST density table was added to the report's source subset;
the public catalogue and detector design parameters remain unchanged.

Figure 2.1 adds positive-side cable envelopes for all four barrel layers, schematic
cooling paths and extraction detail. Figure 2.5 projects all 82 exact terminal cable
sectors and has a color legend; Figure 2.8 gains a color legend. Figure 2.3 keeps its
quantitative stack and adds the PR #8 common accessible-edge panel showing pads,
wire access, discrete illustrative bumps and coverlay construction. The optional
two-chip/alternative panels are omitted. The adapted SVG and its pinned original
hash are retained. No manufactured bump/loop dimensions are inferred.
